title: Price relief on HMO straight-tip catheter charges after a CGM hardship approval: Urology and Continence Supply Program
content:
The price of a non-covered straight-tip intermittent catheter (A4351) charge on the Continence Commercial HMO Program of the Urology and Continence Supply Program reflects financial assistance the customer has on their Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program. The rule reads the hardship applications on that program.

## Price relief

- When the customer's Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program carries a hardship application that is approved and was received within the last 6 calendar months, the price is reduced to half: it is multiplied by 0.5.
- When the newest such approved application was received within the last 12 calendar months but not the last 6, the price is reduced to three quarters: it is multiplied by 0.75.
- Otherwise the price stays the cash price.

The newest approved application is the approved hardship application with the latest received date on the customer's Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program. An application is within the last 6 calendar months when it was received fewer than 6 whole calendar months before the date the charge is settled. The 12-month window is read the same way.

## Boundaries (hypothetical; charge settled on 15 October)

| Newest approved CGM hardship application received | Price multiplied by |
|---|---|
| 16 April of the same year | 0.5 (5 whole months) |
| 15 April of the same year | 0.75 (6 whole months) |
| 16 October of the previous year | 0.75 (11 whole months) |
| 15 October of the previous year | no reduction (12 whole months) |
